A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Soft-Di[M]O work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, including ImageNet results, text-to-image evaluations, refinement ablations, and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds sampling comparisons, concentration diagnostics, runtime measurements, and a Di[M]O variant evaluation.

M1.justification: The main GAN, reward-refinement, and TTEO pipeline is retained. Appendix I.15 adds a tested Di[M]O variant that substitutes masked soft embeddings for sampled tokens in teacher and auxiliary forward passes, explicitly without backpropagating through that substitution.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same class-to-image and text-to-image coverage, including ImageNet-256, LAION-Aesthetics prompts, DALLE3-1M, COCO-30K, MJHQ-30K, GenEval, and HPS evaluations. The added analyses introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: The external baseline sets in the existing benchmark comparisons are unchanged. New Tables 14–15 evaluate argmax against categorical decoding and a soft-embedding Di[M]O variant against standard Di[M]O. REINFORCE is discussed theoretically, not newly evaluated experimentally.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce categorical-versus-argmax evaluation with FID-50K, token-averaged entropy and top-1 probability tracking, and runtime measurements with batch size four per prompt. Existing benchmark protocols and training budgets remain unchanged; the expanded model specifications are additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Appendices I.13–I.15 substantially extend mechanism validation through decoding ablation, concentration trajectories, and testing soft embeddings inside Di[M]O without downstream refinement losses. Appendix I.8 also supplements the retained TTEO/BoN quality analysis with measured runtime costs. Earlier ablations and failure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-training-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The four-start BoN setting was already disclosed in v1. The new theoretical gradient-variance discussion and token-entropy measurements do not change experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but substantial diagnostic and efficiency results are added. Table 14 reports argmax FID 1.57 versus categorical sampling's 1.56; Table 15 reports soft-embedding Di[M]O FID 3.33 versus standard Di[M]O's 2.89. Table 6 reports 5.66 seconds per prompt for four-start, four-iteration TTEO versus 8.57 for BoN-64, replacing v1's approximate runtime-equivalence statement. New curves report concentration and convergence behavior.

T1.justification: v2 adds Section 3.1.3 and Appendix G, absent from v1. These introduce formal objectives, covariance and smoothness assumptions, Lemma G.3's claimed soft-embedding bias bound, Lemma G.4's Gumbel-ST bias argument, proofs, and conditional gradient-variance analysis.

C1.justification: The main application and performance contributions, including ImageNet FID 1.56, are retained. v2 adds explicit small-bias and low-variance claims to the abstract and introduction and foregrounds theoretical justification in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds covariance and forward/backward-mismatch explanations for surrogate behavior. Appendix I.15 interprets the new variant's precision/recall tradeoff as a possible smoothing effect. The retained mode-collapse limitation is narrowed to 'only a small portion in practice,' without a quantified frequency.

D1.justification: Table 5 expands v1's hyperparameter table with image resolutions, sequence lengths, vocabulary sizes, downsampling factors, output dimensions, and MaskBit vocabulary grouping. v2 also specifies the four rewards used for TTEO sample selection and the timing batch size. Code/checkpoint release promises remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gu et al. (2022), Vector Quantized Diffusion Model for Text-to-Image Synthesis. The new theory further contrasts soft embeddings with already-discussed estimators, while Appendix E and the principal novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The methods section gains introduction, benefits, and theory subsections, with the three refinement techniques grouped under Section 3.2. v2 updates the appendix roadmap, selected explanations, acknowledgements, and conference header. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with estimator and runtime tables, sampling and variant-result tables, concentration plots, a comparative pipeline diagram, and a convergence plot. The configuration table is expanded and appendix displays rearranged. Existing benchmark tables and generated-image examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and empirical support through configuration details, runtime measurements, and targeted ablations. However, its newly foregrounded theory is flawed as written: Lemma G.3 equates expected squared deviation with covariance spectral norm rather than trace, and Lemma G.4's mismatch argument does not establish nonvanishing gradient bias. These documentation and empirical gains coexist with reduced theoretical reliability, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
